competition: Paraguayan National Mathematical Olympiad (OMAPA) — Final, Level 3

problems.problem: A store contains many empty cans in four colours: red, green, blue and yellow. Some children build towers with one can on each level and no two cans of the same colour. The towers may have any positive height. How many different towers can be built?
Find the four smallest four-digit numbers that leave remainder $1$ when divided by any of $2,3,4,5,6$.
Find a ten-digit number with no zero digit that is divisible by the sum of its digits.

A parallelogram $ABCD$ has area $60\text{ cm}^2$. A line through $D$ meets $BC$ at $P$ and the extension of $AB$ at $Q$. If quadrilateral $ABPD$ has area $46\text{ cm}^2$, find the area of triangle $CPQ$.

A clinic near a school has $12$ dentists. The $29$ students in the fifth year visit the clinic. Each dentist treats at least two students. Determine the largest number of students that a single dentist can treat.

In the rectangular parallelepiped shown, the lengths $EH,HG,EG$ are consecutive integers. The height is $12$. Find its volume.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/py_2002_p2_fig.png

Six-digit multiples of $3$ are written using three distinct digits. One digit occupies the units position, another the hundreds position, and the third all the remaining positions. If the hundreds digit is decreased by $2$ and the units digit is increased by $2$, all six digits become equal. Find the numbers.
Find all natural numbers $n$ for which $n+195$ and $n-274$ are perfect cubes.

In a trapezoid $ABCD$, side $DA$ is perpendicular to the bases $AB$ and $CD$. The lengths are $AB=45$, $CD=20$ and $BC=65$. Point $P$ lies on $BC$ with $BP=45$, and $M$ is the midpoint of $DA$. Find $PM$.
How many integers greater than $1000$ and less than $10000$ have digit product $256$?

Three distinct nonzero digits are used to form all six three-digit numbers with distinct digits. Their sum is $4218$. The sum of the three largest numbers minus the sum of the three smallest is $792$. Find the three digits.
Writing Pedro's current age followed by Luisa's current age gives a four-digit perfect square. Doing the same in $33$ years would again give a four-digit perfect square. Find their current ages.

Triangle $ABC$ is divided into six smaller triangles by three lines passing through its vertices and a common interior point. The areas of four of the triangles are shown. Find the area of triangle $ABC$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/py_2003_p4_fig.png
In square $ABCD$, $E$ is the midpoint of $BC$. Line $AE$ meets line $DC$ at $F$ and diagonal $BD$ at $G$. If triangle $EFC$ has area $8$, find the area of triangle $GBE$.

Staircases are built from bricks as shown. If $2004$ bricks are available to build a staircase, (a) how many steps will it have, and (b) how many bricks will be left over?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/py_2004_p1_fig.png
Determine the values of $x$ for which $2x+2$, $x+4$ and $x+2$ can be the side lengths of a right triangle.

An equilateral triangle $ABC$ has side length $4$. Draw the line through $A$ perpendicular to $AB$, the line through $B$ perpendicular to $BC$, and the line through $C$ perpendicular to $CA$. These three lines form another triangle. Find its perimeter.
In square $ABCD$, $E$ is the midpoint of $BC$ and $F$ is the midpoint of $CD$. Prove that $AF$ and $AE$ divide diagonal $BD$ into three equal segments.
An integer $A$ has the property that $A^2$ is a four-digit number whose tens digit is $5$. Find all possible values of $A$.
Three-digit numbers are written using digits from $1,2,\ldots,9$, with digit sum $17$. How many numbers can be written?
The number of faces of a pyramid multiplied by its number of edges is $5100$. Find the number of faces.

The complete list of three-digit palindromes is written in increasing order:
$$101,111,121,131,\ldots,979,989,999.$$
Eight consecutive palindromes are deleted. The sum of those remaining is $46150$. Find the eight deleted palindromes.
In the equation $$t=\frac{8a+1}{b},$$ the numbers $a,b,t$ are positive integers and $b<7$. Determine the values of $a$ and $b$ for which $t$ satisfies these conditions.

Let $PQ$ be a chord of a circle and $M$ its midpoint. Two other chords $AB$ and $CD$ pass through $M$. Lines $AC$ and $BD$ meet line $PQ$ at $X$ and $Y$, respectively. Prove that $X$ and $Y$ are equidistant from $M$.
What are the last two digits, the tens and units digits, of $21^{2006}$?
Consider right triangles with integer side lengths whose hypotenuse has a length consecutive to that of one of the legs. How many such triangles exist?

The three circles shown are tangent to lines $L$ and $M$, with each consecutive pair of circles tangent to each other. Their points of tangency with $M$ are $A,B,C$. The smallest circle has radius $12$ and the largest has radius $75$. Find (a) the radius of the middle circle, and (b) the distance from $A$ to the intersection of $L$ and $M$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/py_2006_p3_fig.png

Consider pairs of positive integers $(a,b)$ with $a<b$ satisfying $$\sqrt a+\sqrt b=\sqrt{2160}.$$
Determine all possible values of $a$.
In triangle $ABC$, point $P$ lies on $BC$ with $BP/PC=1/2$. If $\angle ABC=45^\circ$ and $\angle APC=60^\circ$, find $\angle ACB$. A solution using trigonometry is not accepted.

A list of $2007$ natural numbers has average $12$. Seven consecutive entries are deleted, leaving an average of $11.915$. Each of the seven deleted numbers, from the second onwards, is twice its predecessor. Find the seven deleted numbers.

A square $ABCD$ has integer side length and is partitioned into $89$ smaller squares. Of these, $88$ have side length $1$, and the remaining square has an integer side length greater than $1$. Find all possible side lengths of $ABCD$.

In square $ABCD$, points $E$ and $F$ are the midpoints shown, and $P$ is the intersection shown. (a) Prove that $DE\perp CF$. (b) Determine the ratio $CF:PC:EP$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/py_2007_p3_fig.png

Place the numbers $1,2,3,4,5,6,7$, one in each circle of the diagram, so that the sum on every line containing three circles is the same. Which number cannot be placed in circle $E$? For example, $A,D,E$ are aligned, as are $D,C,B$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/py_2007_p4_fig.png
Three equal circles have a common point and also intersect pairwise at $A,B,C$. Prove that their radius equals the circumradius of triangle $ABC$, and that their common point is its orthocenter.
How many positive integers less than $500$ have no prime factors other than $2,7,11$?

Let $$S=|n-1|+|n-2|+\cdots+|n-100|,$$ where $n$ is an integer with $1<n<100$. Determine the values of $n$ for which $S$ is smallest. Here $|A|$ denotes the absolute value of $A$, for example $|-2|=2$.

In an isosceles triangle $ABC$, $AB=AC$ and $BC=12$. Let $D$ be the midpoint of $BC$. The perpendicular through $D$ to $AC$ meets $AC$ at $E$. Point $F$ lies on $AB$ with $EF\parallel BC$. If $EC=4$, find $EF$.

In the diagram, $AB$ and $AC$ are tangents to a circle at $B$ and $C$. Point $P$ lies on the circle. Draw $PD,PE,PF$ perpendicular to $BC,AC,AB$, respectively. Prove that $PD^2=PE\cdot PF$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/py_2008_p4_fig.png
Let $m,n,p$ be rational numbers such that $\sqrt m+\sqrt n+\sqrt p$ is rational. Prove that $\sqrt m$, $\sqrt n$ and $\sqrt p$ are rational.
In triangle $ABC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$. A circle with diameter $BC$ meets $AB$ at $D$. Its tangent at $D$ meets $AC$ at $F$. If $\angle CAB=46^\circ$, find $\angle CFD$.
How many positive integers $n\le2009$ have the property that the last digit of $n^{20}$ is $1$?
A sequence has the property that the average of its first $n$ terms is $n$, for $n=1,2,3,\ldots$. Find the sum of its first $2009$ terms.

In triangle $ABC$, the incenter $I$ is at distance $4\text{ cm}$ from side $BC$ and $12\text{ cm}$ from vertex $B$. Inside angle $ABC$, choose a point $D$ that is the center of a circle tangent to lines $AB$ and $BC$ and passing through $I$. Find all possible distances $DB$.

Juan wants to divide a square field among his three children as shown, because a well at vertex $B$ must be shared. The field has side length $60\text{ m}$. Each child is to receive the same area. At what distances from vertex $D$ should points $M$ and $N$ lie?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/py_2010_p1_fig.png

The diagram shows figures constructed according to a rule that you must discover. How many unit squares will the figure contain after $20$ steps?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/py_2010_p2_fig.png
In triangle $ABC$, draw median $BM$. Suppose that $BC=\frac23MC$ and $\angle BMC=2\angle ABM$. Find $AB/AM$.
Find all four-digit natural numbers $\overline{abcd}$ that are multiples of $11$, for which the two-digit number $\overline{ac}$ is a multiple of $7$ and $a+b+c+d=d^2$.

In triangle $ABC$, draw altitudes $AD,BE,CF$. Extend them to meet the circumcircle again at points different from $A,B,C$. Prove that the triangle formed by these three further intersection points is similar to triangle $DEF$.
Evaluate $$\frac12+\left(\frac13+\frac23\right)+\left(\frac14+\frac24+\frac34\right)+\cdots+\left(\frac1{1000}+\frac2{1000}+\cdots+\frac{999}{1000}\right).$$
In triangle $ABC$, draw medians $BD$ and $AE$. The distance between the midpoints of these medians is $4.5$. Find $AB$.

Dividing the four-digit number $\overline{aaaa}$ by the two-digit number $\overline{bb}$ gives a quotient between $140$ and $160$, inclusive, and remainder $\overline{(a-b)(a-b)}$, the two-digit number whose two digits are both $a-b$. Find all pairs $(a,b)$ satisfying this condition.
A natural number $N$ is divided into $n$ parts inversely proportional to $2,6,12,20,\ldots$. The smallest part equals $N/400$. Find $n$.

In a right triangle, the segment joining the incenter and centroid is parallel to one of the legs and has length $10\text{ cm}$. Find the lengths of the legs. The incenter is the intersection of the angle bisectors and the centroid is the intersection of the medians.
A list begins with a one-digit natural number. Each subsequent number is obtained by adding $9$ to the previous one. The number $2012$ occurs in the list. Find its first number.

A travelling ant moves on a black-and-white checkerboard, horizontally or vertically, without visiting a square more than once. From which squares can it start and visit every square of the board if the board is (a) $4\times4$, (b) $5\times5$, and (c) $n\times n$, where $n$ is any natural number?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/py_2012_p2_fig.png

A triangle $ABC$, right-angled at $B$, is inscribed in a semicircle with diameter $AC=10$. Find the distance from $B$ to $AC$ if the median to $AC$ is the geometric mean of the other two sides. Recall that $n$ is the geometric mean of $m$ and $q$ when $m/n=n/q$.

Find the four-digit number $\overline{abcd}$ with four distinct digits that is divisible by $3$ and satisfies $\overline{ab}-\overline{cd}=11$. Here $\overline{ab}$ and $\overline{cd}$ denote two-digit numbers.
In equilateral triangle $ABC$, choose a point $Q$ on $BC$. Extend $AQ$ to meet the circumcircle at $P$. Prove that $$\frac1{PB}+\frac1{PC}=\frac1{PQ}.$$
Triangle $ABC$ has area $9$. Points $M,N$ are the midpoints of $AB,AC$, respectively. Point $P$ lies on $BC$ with $PC=BC/3$. Lines $PN$ and $CM$ meet at $O$. Find the area of quadrilateral $BPOM$.
A $k$-digit natural number $N$ is divided by $19$. Its remainder is $10^{k-2}-Q$, where $Q$ is the quotient, $Q<101$, and $10^{k-2}-Q>0$. How many possible values can $N$ have?

Pedro and Juan play with two piles containing $X$ and $Y$ stones, where $X<12$ and $Y<11$. On a turn, a player may remove one stone from one pile, two stones from one pile, one stone from each pile, or two stones from one pile and one from the other. A player must remove stones on each turn. The player who removes the last stone loses. Pedro moves first and has a winning strategy. What are the three largest possible values of $X+Y$?

In an obtuse triangle $ABC$, $AB$ is the longest side. Draw the bisector of $\angle BAC$ and let the perpendiculars to it from $B,C$ have feet $P,Q$, respectively. Point $D$ lies on line $BC$ with $AD\perp AP$. Prove that lines $AD,BQ,PC$ are concurrent.

The figure shows a square with side length $12\text{ cm}$. Irina draws another square whose perimeter is $8\text{ cm}$ greater. What is the area of Irina's square?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/py_2014_p1_fig.png
Clau writes all four-digit natural numbers in which digits $3$ and $7$ must occur next to each other. How many digits does she write in total?

Juan chooses a five-digit positive integer. María deletes its units digit, obtaining a four-digit number. The sum of this four-digit number and the original five-digit number is $52713$. What can the sum of the original number's five digits be?

Nair and Yuli play on a row of $203$ squares with one token. Initially the token is in the first square from the left. Nair moves first. On each turn a player moves the token $1$, $2$ or $3$ squares to the right. The first player to reach the last square wins. What strategy should Nair use to guarantee victory?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/py_2014_p4_fig.png
Triangle $ABC$ has area $92\text{ cm}^2$. Find the area of a triangle whose side lengths equal the lengths of the medians of $ABC$.

Alexa writes the first $16$ terms of a sequence:
$$1,2,2,3,4,4,5,6,6,7,8,8,9,10,10,11,\ldots.$$
She continues the same pattern until she has written $2015$ terms. What is the last term?
How many sums of fewer than $10$ consecutive positive integers have value $2015$?

A cube is divided into eight equal smaller cubes as shown. Each resulting cube is then divided into eight cubes again. This process is repeated four more times on each resulting cube. What is the ratio of the sum of the total surface areas of all the cubes from the last division to the surface area of the original cube?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/py_2015_p3_fig.png
The side lengths of a triangle are natural-number multiples of $7$, less than $40$. How many different triangles satisfy these conditions?

The diagram shows a rectangle made of four equal smaller rectangles. There are $10$ rectangles in the diagram in total. How many rectangles would there be in a rectangle formed in the same way from $n$ smaller rectangles?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/py_2015_p5_fig.png

A river is crossed simultaneously by $203$ people. Of these, $63$ travel in boats of capacity $7$ and $42$ in boats of capacity $6$. Of the remaining people, one group uses only boats of capacity $4$ and the other only boats of capacity $3$. Every boat is full without exceeding its capacity. What is the smallest possible number of boats used?
Find all integer pairs $(a,b)$ satisfying $5a+7b=41$, $-11<a<5$ and $2<b<14$.

All vertices of a polygon lie on a circle. Joining each vertex to the center forms isosceles triangles as shown. All three angles of each triangle are integer numbers of degrees. The central angles are pairwise distinct and are multiples of the smallest central angle. If the polygon contains the largest possible number of these isosceles triangles, (a) what is the smallest central angle, and (b) how many sides does the polygon have?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/py_2016_p3_fig.png

Pedro has $75$ bars of different sizes, some white and some black. One white bar has the same size as two black bars together. Another white bar, smaller than the preceding bars, has the same size as three black bars together. A third white bar, smaller than all those previously listed, has the same size as four black bars together, and so on. How many white bars are there?

There are $n$ squares standing on the same line. Draw a line from the bottom-left vertex of the first square to the top-right vertex of the last, as shown. The numbers below the diagram give the side lengths of the first four squares. Determine the shaded area in terms of $n$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/py_2016_p5_fig.png
